name: Run handoff confirmed → dispatched → executing
description:
The dispatched→executing bridge, half 2 (the run-entity transition). ported from semteams agent-run/02. Fires on the RUN entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>) when half 1 (01-handoff-marker) has stamped agent.run.handoff there AND the run is still in `dispatched`, and advances it to `executing` via lifecycle_transition (the firing entity IS the run entity, which is what the action transitions). Reaching `executing` is what makes the run's work 'in flight' and lets the downstream run-lifecycle gates (offer-change-approval, …) evaluate.

The phase guard (agent.run.phase == dispatched) is a TOP-LEVEL CONDITION, not an action `when`, so the rule simply does not match until the edge is legal — the illegal dispatched→X is never attempted (no ErrInvalidTransition, no lost transition). The processor re-evaluates every entity-state rule on each KV revision, so the transition fires exactly once when both the handoff marker and the dispatched phase hold.

The run.awaiting.human length_eq 0 guard is the D15 park-exclusion contract (a conformance pin enforces it on every lifecycle_transition rule): a run parked toward a human must not be swept through this advance before the human-resume path clears the marker. A freshly-minted run carries no awaiting_human, so this never blocks the normal path; it only holds a run that parked between mint and advance.

on_enter.reason: child task handed off (rule.task.spawned confirmed) — run is now executing

metadata.fires_on: the run entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>), evaluated on the beta.147 entity-state lane via this rule's entity.pattern (watch-all; conditions do the discrimination).
metadata.phase_guard_is_condition: agent.run.phase == dispatched is a top-level condition so the invalid edge is never attempted.
